newsitem.title: UK: Troubled Anglo announces bank restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Anglo announces bank restructuring.

text.p: Troubled fuels and general trading group Anglo-United Plc said on Thursday it expected a restructuring of its finances to take place in the autumn.

Earlier the British-based company, which has trading interests in the Falkland Islands, announced the sale of its UK smokeless fuel and chemicals manufacturer Coalite Products Ltd to Thomas Potts Plc for 24.3 million stg ($39.8 million).
However, Anglo said that after the sale its total liabilities would "remain significantly greater than its total assets", with bank debts of 178 million stg and net assets of 35 million stg.
The company has not made a profit since 1992.
Under the plan, Anglo said it expected its bankers to convert loan notes and long-term loans into new shares in Anglo, doubling the number of shares in issue to around 1.8 billion.
Anglo shares, which surged to a high of 3 pence in March, were trading at 1 penny midmorning, down 0.75.

Shares will be exchanged for shares in a new company, the Falkland Islands group, which will consist of Anglo's three Falkland Islands operations. Non-bank shareholders will own just over 25 percent of the new company.
Anglo said that without the sale of Coalite "there are no realistic prospects of Anglo extricating itself from its current adverse financial position".
